doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Overseas in the Pacific and a close call
summary: He declines to discuss Australia exploits but praises the service and mentions a near-death time.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And you eventually went overseas in Southeast Asia?
Oh yeah. We won’t get into that. The exploits in Australia and so on. That’s not something we’ll talk about.
No? Not even in part two of our interview?
No, but it was a wonderful experience, wonderful people. I never met a single person I didn’t like in the service, in the submarine service. It was a great experience.
Was there ever a time when you didn’t think you were going to come back from that?
Yeah. That wasn’t such a good experience. That was a time that we call brownie shorts. You know I had one of those.
